title: Choose the Workspace's new visual world — safer register
question: You steered toward the familiar end. These are the three most conventional grounded directions still on the table, plus the category standard for comparison. Lock one, or steer again.

options.label: Le Relevé du Trésor Public
options.thesis: Every workbook is a line in the agency's own treasury statement — débit/crédit-style columns make status and ownership read like a financial record, not a file list.
options.viewport: A ruled statement header (agency letterhead band), then rows: reference no., libellé (programme name), a débit/crédit-style sync indicator, date, agent responsible.
options.risk: Familiar almost to the point of being invisible — the safest, least distinctive reading of 'government finance register.'

regions.label: ruled rows: ref | libellé | débit/crédit sync | date | agent

options.label: Le Bordereau de Transmission
options.thesis: Each workbook carries its own transmittal slip — a strip of checkboxes showing which stage (edited, synced, reported) it has passed through.
options.viewport: A slim header, then rows of transmittal slips: reference no., programme title, a row of stage checkboxes initialed when passed, date, destinataire.
options.risk: Reads over-bureaucratic if every row shows the full multi-stage checklist even for a workbook with nothing pending.

regions.label: slip rows: ref | programme | stage checkboxes | date | destinataire

options.label: Le Répertoire du Hall
options.thesis: The workspace is the building's own lobby directory — services and their current workbook listed by engraved plate, updated by sliding in a fresh nameplate.
options.viewport: A single engraved directory panel: rows of channel-mounted nameplates, one per workbook, sliding in updated titles and programme codes.
options.risk: The most static-feeling of the three — a physical directory board doesn't obviously suggest live, frequently-edited data unless the update motion is deliberate.

regions.label: channel-mounted nameplate rows, one per workbook

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What Google Drive, SharePoint document libraries, and Airtable's grid view all ship for a file list — executed at their own craft level, no irony.
canonCard.viewport: Greeting hero, upload dropzone, sparse card grid of files below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any other SaaS console — exactly what this redesign is meant to move away from.
